ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit fault. Sensor reading outside expected range — either sensor has failed or wiring harness has a fault. ECU cannot accurately determine engine temperature, affecting fuel mixture calculations.
ai_diagnosis.immediate_action: Monitor engine temperature via dashboard gauge. If gauge shows overheating, stop vehicle immediately. Avoid extended highway driving until sensor is replaced.
ai_diagnosis.long_term_fix: Replace coolant temperature sensor. Inspect wiring harness for chafing or corrosion at connector. Clear fault code and verify sensor reads within normal range after replacement.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Random cylinder misfire detected. Low battery voltage combined with high coolant temperature is destabilising the ignition system. Most likely cause: failing alternator unable to maintain charge under thermal load.
ai_diagnosis.immediate_action: Reduce engine load immediately. Avoid high RPM driving. Schedule workshop inspection within 48 hours. Do not drive on motorway until voltage issue resolved.
ai_diagnosis.long_term_fix: Test alternator output voltage at operating temperature. Replace alternator if output below 13.5V. Inspect cooling system for thermostat failure.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Lost CAN bus communication with Engine Control Module. Critical network fault — ECM has powered down unexpectedly or CAN bus wiring has failed. Multiple vehicle safety systems affected.
ai_diagnosis.immediate_action: Stop vehicle safely immediately. Do not attempt restart without professional diagnosis. Multiple safety systems may be impaired. Call for recovery.
ai_diagnosis.long_term_fix: Inspect CAN bus wiring harness at ECM connector. Check termination resistors (60 ohms between CAN-H and CAN-L). Verify ECM power supply and ground connections.
